## Install

```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.add(url = "https://github.com/andrerecio/LocalProjections.jl")
```

This is a fork of Giuseppe Ragusa's
[LocalProjections.jl](https://github.com/gragusa/LocalProjections.jl). It
adds HAR inference with equal-weighted-cosine (EWC) variances and Student-$t$
critical values, the Herbst–Johannsen bias correction, the VAR moving-block
bootstrap, VAR lag selection, and state-dependent projections.

## The workflow in a few lines

```julia
using LocalProjections, StatsModels, CovarianceMatrices, Plots
r = lp(@formula(leads(y) ~ shock + lags(y, 4) + lags(shock, 4)), df; horizon = 20)
summarize(r, Bartlett{NeweyWest}(); level = 0.90)   # path, s.e. and bands
plot(r, EWC(ewc_bandwidth(r)); levels = [0.68, 0.90])
```

The left-hand side sets the response: `leads(y)` for $y_{t+h}$, `cumul(y)` for
$\sum_{j \le h} y_{t+j}$, `anchor(y, z)` for $y_{t+h} - z_t$. `lpiv` takes an
instrumented regressor, `(cumul(g) ~ z)`, and the covariance estimator is any
estimator from CovarianceMatrices.jl.

## Rebuilding these pages

From `docs/quarto/`:

```sh
julia --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()'
quarto render
```

Computed results are frozen in `_freeze/`, so a page is re-run only when its
source changes. A change to the package itself does not invalidate them:
re-render a page explicitly (`quarto render ramey-zubairy.qmd` always
executes) or delete `_freeze/`. This build:
LocalProjections at commit `{julia} commit`, Julia `{julia} string(VERSION)`.
